raw_segments.text: According to the eloquent, and sometimes well-informed, author of the philosophical and political
history of the establishment of the Europeans in the two Indies, the annual importation
of registered gold and silver into Spain, at an average of eleven years, viz. from 1754
to 1764, both inclusive, amounted to 13,984,185 piesters of ten reels.
On account of what may have been smuggled, however, the whole annual importation, he
supposes, may have amounted to 17 millions of piesters, which at fours.
6d. The piester is equal to 3,825,000 pounds sterling. He gives the detail two of the
particular places from which the gold and silver were brought, and of the particular
quantities of each metal, which according to the register, each of them afforded.
He informs us, too, that if we were to judge of the quantity of gold annually imported
from the Brazil's to Lisbon, by the amount of the tax paid to the King of Portugal, which
it seems, is one-fifth of the standard metal, we might value it at eighteen millions of
cruzados, or forty-five millions of French livers, equal to about twenty million sterling.
On account of what may have been smuggled, however, we may safely, he says, add to this
250,000 pounds sterling, so that the whole will amount to 2,250,000 pounds sterling.
According to this account, therefore, the whole annual importation of the precious metals
into both Spain and Portugal, mounts to about 6,075,000 pounds sterling.
